transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble sitting through things. What finally pushed me to make an appointment is... well, I keep getting up during important things. Like sprint planning for work, or... I had these mortgage calls recently. 

I know I should just stay put, but I'll just... suddenly decide I need water, or I'll feel like I have to go check something in the other room. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When you get up during these meetings or calls, is it because you suddenly feel you need to check something to stop a bad outcome from happening?
Um... no. Not really. It's not about... preventing anything bad from happening. I just... I don't know, I just get up.
When you get up during these meetings or calls, is it because you suddenly feel a surge of panic?
No, it's not panic. I just... I don't know, I just feel restless, I guess. It's not a panic attack or anything.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high-energy compared with your normal self?
Um... no. I don't think so. I'm pretty much always just... like this. I haven't noticed any weird spikes in energy or anything.
Does this restlessness happen in other situations too, not just work meetings or phone calls?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... even if I'm just sitting there, looking calm on the outside... I still get this pressure inside. Like I just need to move, or... do something with my hands, or switch to a different task. It just... it feels like I'm going to crawl out of my skin if I don't.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on what someone is saying, even when you want to pay attention?
Um... no, not really. I can usually follow a conversation fine. I haven't noticed any issues with that.
When you feel this restlessness, is it usually happening because your mind is full of worry?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I'm worrying about anything when it happens. It's just... a physical feeling, I guess.
Did you feel this same kind of restlessness when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Um... in elementary school, my teachers were always... moving my desk around. They had to remind me to stay in my seat a lot. I guess I was always getting up, or... blurting things out before it was my turn. And I'd rush through my work, even if I knew how to do it. So... yeah, it's been around for a while.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of hyperactivity/impulsivity: difficulty remaining seated, inner restlessness, needing to move, blurting out answers, and rushing through work. Symptoms occur across settings and are not better explained by panic, obsessive fears, generalized worry, or episodic elevated energy. Although inattentive symptoms were not endorsed, the confirmed presentation is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type.
